method: Started from 6,053 priced Kalshi legs in the next 36 hours. Kept legs priced 30–85¢ with edge of about −2.5 or better and no flags, one per game, and matched them against today's 205 newly collected expert picks (plus yesterday's picks for games still to come) and Polymarket top-trader positions. A leg stayed only if at least two of top-trader money, a published pick or model, and concrete matchup/injury reasoning agreed, with nothing disagreeing. Dropped for conflicts: Tennessee +2.5 vs LSU (eight outlets on the Vols, but $7.6k of top-trader money on LSU −1.5); Georgia −15.5 (six outlets, but Doc's Sports takes South Carolina and top traders are against Georgia at −16.5/−17.5); UCLA −3.5, Arsenal ML and Texas Tech −3.5 (experts for, top traders against); Utah ML at TCU (experts split on the spread); Bears −9.5 (three outlets on the Saints); Texas A&M/Oklahoma (experts split); Buffalo ML at Florida (top traders against). Sunday NBA, NHL and college basketball had no published picks yet, so the ladder leans on Saturday college football/NBA/NHL plus Sunday Premier League and NFL; NFL Sunday is Week 11.
honest: Every leg costs slightly more than its fair price (edge about −0.2 to −2.4¢ each), so expected return is slightly negative, and it gets worse with each leg you add.

ladder.label: Milwaukee Bucks +11.5
ladder.why: Philadelphia is without Jaylen Brown (hamstring) and Tyrese Maxey is questionable; the 76ers' average margin is only about +2.9 with just two 12+ point wins, and Milwaukee's last five losses were all by 11 or fewer. Five outlets take the Bucks with the points and top-trader money is on Milwaukee +11.5 and +12.5.

ladder.label: Liverpool
ladder.why: Manchester United are in the drop zone, winless in eight, and Pochettino takes charge for the first time with Sesko, Baleba and Ugarte out; van Dijk and Szoboszlai are fit for Liverpool. Four previews pick a Liverpool win and top-trader money is on Liverpool.

ladder.label: Under 47.5
ladder.why: Arkansas's offense ranks 109th in success rate and has scored 23 or fewer in three of its last five, against a Texas defense allowing 17.8 points a game. Two outlets take the Under and top-trader money is on it too.

ladder.label: Under 228.5
ladder.why: Minnesota is without Anthony Edwards (knee surgery), DiVincenzo and Jaylen Clark, and Memphis is missing Jerami Grant, Boozer and GG Jackson; only 3 of 10 Wolves home games have gone over. Predictem takes the Under and top-trader money is $2.8k on it vs $0.1k against.

ladder.label: Arizona Wildcats −7.5
ladder.why: Kansas State is without QB Avery Johnson, while Arizona's Fifita-led offense ranks 8th in EPA per dropback. Covers takes Arizona −7.5 and top-trader money leans the same way ($2.5k for vs $0.6k against).

ladder.label: Missouri Tigers
ladder.why: Kentucky's pass defense and success-rate numbers are weak, and Missouri's passing game should exploit it. numberFire gives Missouri about 66% to win, and Covers and SI both lay the points with the Tigers.

ladder.label: Calgary Flames
ladder.why: Chicago is 6-14-2, winless on the road (0-8-1) and 31st in goals for and against, and Connor Bedard is out with a shoulder injury. Two outlets pick Calgary to win.

sources.name: Sports Betting Dime / Michael Schwartz (Flames ML)

ladder.label: Brighton & Hove Albion
ladder.why: Hull are nine Premier League games without a win and missing Targett, Morita and Matazo, while Brighton come in on a three-game winning run (though without Mitoma and Ferguson). Two previews pick a Brighton away win.

ladder.label: Under 44.5
ladder.why: Minnesota's defense has produced eight straight unders and the 49ers allow just 3.4 yards per carry; Predictem projects 23-17. Two outlets take the Under.

ladder.label: Dallas Cowboys
ladder.why: Dallas ranks 5th in scoring and Tennessee's offense 28th. CBS and Pickswise lay the points with Dallas (Covers takes Tennessee +7.5 but not to win), and top-trader money is $30k on Dallas vs $3.7k on Tennessee.

ladder.label: Denver Broncos
ladder.why: The Raiders start rookie Fernando Mendoza, sacked six times in his debut, against Denver's pass rush. Covers lays −10.5 with Denver; Predictem and Pickswise take the Raiders with the points but still project a Denver win (Predictem 23-17).
